transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-22 14:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Lena (BlueForge Head of Alliances), Brian (BlueForge SA), Maya (BlueForge Sales Dir), Jordan (BlueForge Partner Ops).

[00:00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call — we can do a 60 second objective: align on accounts, figure out velocity blockers, and carve out who runs the pilot.
[00:00:24] Lena (BlueForge): Yep that's perfect. We're trying to accelerate a few EMEA and NA deals this quarter so anything that speeds the handoff helps.
[00:00:36] Maya (BlueForge): Also want to make sure we have an exec sponsor intro baked in — that tends to unblock procurement.
[00:00:50] Diego (Redwood SE): Cool, from a tech side we want to validate two things: first latency/cost envelope on BlueForge infra, and second that our routing/fallbacks work across your node pools.
[00:01:12] Brian (BlueForge): On infra, we're running mixed A100 and H100 in NA, and Ampere-type inference in EMEA — some hetero stuff. Expect some variance.
[00:01:30] Priya (Redwood CSM): Noted. For the pilot success template I can propose SLOs — p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy regression tolerances.
[00:01:45] Jordan (BlueForge): Quick question: where does ownership sit during a handoff? BlueForge SDR passes to our AE, then joint intro with Redwood?
[00:02:02] Avery (Redwood AE): Typically Redwood AE + partner AM do joint intro then SE-led tech scoping. We want to keep the initial demo short, then handoff to pilot.
[00:02:20] Maya (BlueForge): That matches our motion. But we've seen deals slow where we don't get the exec sponsor in the first 2 weeks.
[00:02:35] Avery (Redwood AE): Ok let's make exec intro a formal action item.

[00:03:10] Diego (Redwood SE): Technical note — when we benchmark, we need sample workload: typical concurrency, prompt lengths, and KV cache hit rates. BlueForge, can you give a 48hr sample?
[00:03:28] Brian (BlueForge): We can export a scrubbed trace, yes. Will likely be representative: median prompt 120 tokens, tail at 1.2k tokens on summarize jobs.
[00:03:45] Diego (Redwood SE): Great. Also, we may see transcriptions where KV cache is called "KV cash" in some logs — just flagging that auto transcriptions sometimes swap words.
[00:03:58] Lena (BlueForge): Ha, noted.

[00:05:05] Avery (Redwood AE): Moving to coverage mapping — Jordan, you mentioned a list of top accounts you want to target jointly?
[00:05:13] Jordan (BlueForge): Yes we have a top 12 list, but want to align on which are best for Redwood joint motion. Some are already in outreach with other partners.
[00:05:30] Priya (Redwood CSM): If you share the list we can mark overlap and recommend 6 high-probability targets for Q4. We'll also add suggested plays per account.
[00:05:46] Maya (BlueForge): We also want clarity on which contacts need an SSO/KYC conversation early — procurement locks us until security okays the vendor.
[00:05:59] Avery (Redwood AE): We'll attach our security one-pager and SOC-2 artifacts. We'll also include our Private deployment options for regulated customers.

[00:07:10] Brian (BlueForge): On procurement, what's Redwood's typical timeline for Dedicated vs Hosted? Our legal teams ask different questions.
[00:07:22] Avery (Redwood AE): Hosted is fastest — minutes to spin up for demo. Dedicated takes longer— usually 4–8 weeks with contract and capacity commit. Private/VPC add the security review and can be 8–12 weeks depending on infra.
[00:07:40] Lena (BlueForge): Ok that's useful for expectation setting.

[00:09:00] Diego (Redwood SE): Technical deep dive — when we run the throughput bench, we'll test model combo A (gpt-variant + quantized weights) with batching and prefix cache enabled. We want to show cost delta with and without caching.
[00:09:18] Brian (BlueForge): For EMEA, we might have a slightly different kernel set, so results could vary; please call out hardware in the report.
[00:09:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Absolutely. I'll include p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost-per-10k tokens assumptions.

[00:10:45] Maya (BlueForge): A practical ask — for joint outreach, do you have a co-branded playbook and one-pager? We prefer something our AEs can forward.
[00:11:00] Priya (Redwood CSM): We do have a co-sell starter kit. Avery will share an updated deck with partner-specific slides.
[00:11:10] Avery (Redwood AE): Yep I'll drop a co-branded pitch deck and a one-pager that highlights Dedicated and Private options and the joint support model.

[00:12:40] Jordan (BlueForge): A small red flag we've seen: customers push back on token costs when they see large batch jobs. How do we frame cost savings?
[00:12:52] Diego (Redwood SE): We usually show two numbers: baseline (no batching, no cache) and optimized (batching + cache + quantization). It makes the delta concrete.
[00:13:06] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll also add a recommended pricing conversation script for AEs to use when customers are concerned.

[00:15:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Let's talk about pilot success criteria. Priya, can you outline the recommended template?
[00:15:08] Priya (Redwood CSM): Sure. Template includes: 1) Technical SLOs (p50 < 200ms for short prompts, p95 < 600ms), 2) Cost cap per 1M tokens, 3) Accuracy/regression tolerance measured on a holdout prompt-set, 4) Uptime and fallback behavior, 5) Data handling and retention agreements.
[00:15:38] Brian (BlueForge): Can we be flexible on latency thresholds for longer prompts? Some customers care less about p95 on 1k+ prompts.
[00:15:50] Priya (Redwood CSM): Yes, the template is parameterized by prompt length bins.

[00:17:05] Lena (BlueForge): For enterprise deals, can we request a named SE to support the pilot? It helps with confidence.
[00:17:16] Avery (Redwood AE): We'll assign a dedicated SE for the pilot phase. Diego can lead if schedules align.
[00:17:24] Diego (Redwood SE): Happy to.

[00:18:30] Maya (BlueForge): A few deals have strict data residency — we may need Private deployment in EMEA region. Is that supported?
[00:18:40] Avery (Redwood AE): Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; we can scope that per account. That does add implementation time and a platform fee.
[00:18:55] Lena (BlueForge): Noted. We'll flag those accounts in the list.

[00:20:12] Diego (Redwood SE): Quick architecture question — BlueForge, do you prefer direct peering or transit VPN for pilot connectivity? Peering gives lower latency but requires network setup.
[00:20:25] Jordan (BlueForge): Peering is preferred for high-volume pilots; our infra team can provision by request but it adds a 5–7 day lead.
[00:20:38] Diego (Redwood SE): Ok we'll plan peering for the top 2 pilots and VPN for smaller ones.

[00:21:55] Avery (Redwood AE): Let's surface risk areas — what might slow deals?
[00:22:02] Brian (BlueForge): Security review/attestation timing, exec sponsor unavailability, and unclear ownership during the pilot.
[00:22:14] Maya (BlueForge): Also internal product roadmaps where our customers are evaluating multiple vendor integrations.
[00:22:25] Avery (Redwood AE): Good. We'll mitigate by: sending SOC2 docs up front, formalizing exec-intro and ownership in the win plan, and sharing a short competitive battlecard.

[00:24:10] Priya (Redwood CSM): On success metrics, we should instrument a shared dashboard — Redwood can export token and latency metrics and BlueForge can overlay CRM-stage.
[00:24:24] Jordan (BlueForge): We can accept a read-only dashboard link; please ensure PII isn't in logs.
[00:24:36] Diego (Redwood SE): We'll scrub logs and provide aggregated metrics only.

[00:26:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Ok, account prioritization: Jordan will share top-12, Redwood will mark 6 high probability and return play assignments.
[00:26:12] Jordan (BlueForge): Will do by Friday.

[00:27:40] Maya (BlueForge): A question on pricing: do you discount for co-sell pipeline commitments?
[00:27:50] Avery (Redwood AE): We have partner discount tiers for committed Dedicated capacity and for co-sell pilots tied to revenue share — details in the partner contract. I'll attach the current partner pricing sheet.
[00:28:10] Lena (BlueForge): Great. Please include any minimums.

[00:30:00] Diego (Redwood SE): On the benchmark plan: I'll need a scrubbed trace, expected concurrency, and hardware details. Will run both with caching on and off, and with quantized weights. Expect a short report (PDF) and raw csv.
[00:30:18] Brian (BlueForge): We'll deliver the trace by Wednesday.
[00:30:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Note: kernel selection differences may show up in EMEA results; we'll call that out.

[00:32:05] Priya (Redwood CSM): For enablement, we can run a 45m joint training for BlueForge AEs next week — covers pitch, demo script, and objection handling.
[00:32:18] Maya (BlueForge): Let's do that. Fridays are best.
[00:32:26] Avery (Redwood AE): I'll propose two slots and poll.

[00:34:10] Jordan (BlueForge): Ops note: we need a shared place to drop artifacts — can you use the partner folder on Box?
[00:34:20] Avery (Redwood AE): Yes, we'll use a Box folder and I'll send link.
[00:34:30] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll also add the pilot success template there.

[00:36:00] Brian (BlueForge): One thing — SOC2 scope questions: do you have a SOC2 Type II with encryption details and KMS integration notes?
[00:36:12] Avery (Redwood AE): Yes we do. I'll attach SOC2 and a short KMS integration note. For Private deployments we can also support customer-managed keys in HSM.
[00:36:30] Lena (BlueForge): Good. That will cut cycles in security review.

[00:38:05] Maya (BlueForge): Any notable competitor motions we should arm AEs for?
[00:38:14] Diego (Redwood SE): Customers sometimes ask about Bedrock's managed model roster and Anthropic's safety posture. We should emphasize Redwood's production-grade SLOs, routing/fallbacks, and cost control levers.
[00:38:30] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll add a quick battlecard.

[00:40:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Recap — action items: Avery send deck and pricing; Jordan send top-12; Diego run benchmark; Priya draft pilot template; BlueForge provide trace. Any objections?
[00:40:18] Lena (BlueForge): No objections. Sounds good.
[00:40:26] Jordan (BlueForge): One more ask — can Redwood provide a short case study template we can co-sign after first win?
[00:40:36] Avery (Redwood AE): Yes, we'll include a one-page case study template in the box folder.

[00:42:00] Diego (Redwood SE): Technical aside: for latency numbers, we'll include tokenization assumptions and prompt prefix lengths in the appendix.
[00:42:12] Brian (BlueForge): Helpful.

[00:44:00] Priya (Redwood CSM): I'll spin up the shared success dashboard — request read-only at first.
[00:44:12] Jordan (BlueForge): Fine by us.

[00:46:30] Avery (Redwood AE): Ok last logistics — exec intro target week of 2025-11-03. Avery will coordinate calendars.
[00:46:42] Maya (BlueForge): We can block tentative time.

[00:48:55] Diego (Redwood SE): Any final tech risks?
[00:49:02] Brian (BlueForge): Only potential incompat with a few private kernels, but we'll surface during benchmark.
[00:49:12] Diego (Redwood SE): Got it.

[00:50:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the Box link and the spreadsheet.
[00:50:10] Lena (BlueForge): Thank you.
[00:50:16] Maya (BlueForge): Thanks all.
[00:50:22] Priya (Redwood CSM): Bye.

Meeting notes: references/attachments: https://box.redwood.ai/partners/blueforge-q4 (co-branded deck, pilot template, SOC2 redacted pdf), benchmark-spreadsheet link (private), partner-pricing-sheet.pdf.

End of transcript.
